title: Tighten PowerShell rename filters for leaked release tags
summary: Make pipeline-owned movie and TV destination naming stricter for release groups, video bit-depth tags, upscaled markers, and TV season special markers that leaked into current output paths.
reason: Current output folders included release and metadata tokens such as +SP, TTGA, Asiimov, Rapta, Licdom, 10bits, and UpScaled even though the Settings naming filters were enabled.
behavior_before: PowerShell destination naming could leave selected release groups, video bit-depth plurals, upscaled tags, and TV +SP folder markers in generated Plex movie or TV paths.
behavior_after: PowerShell destination naming strips those tags before composing Plex movie and TV folder/file names.
manual_validation: Direct PowerShell planner check for current leaked movie/TV output names - passed
mediapipeline.tools.dev.refresh_summaries - passed; unrelated pre-existing/generated summary dirt remains outside this packet
rollback_plan: Revert the PowerShell naming filter updates, focused naming support tests, generated summaries, and this change packet.
notes:
Change packet created before implementation on 2026-06-19.
Implementation and focused validation completed on 2026-06-19; strict worktree coverage is blocked by unrelated dirty files listed by validate_changes.
